Here is the commit message:
Fix NPE when stories are run using JUnit runner

jbehave-junit-runner builds JUnit execution tree before the actual
execution. Also it knows nothing about Vividus batches. As result
when BDD stories are run NPE is thrown, because no batch is running.

Here is the root cause:
The `BddRunContext` class stored the currently running batch identifier in a field `runningBatchKey` of type `Optional<String>` that was left uninitialized (defaulting to `null`) until a batch actually started execution via the normal Vividus runner flow (which explicitly sets this field before running stories). However, when tests are executed via the `jbehave-junit-runner`, the JUnit test execution tree is built *before* the actual story execution begins, and this runner has no knowledge of Vividus's batch concept, so it never triggers the code path that initializes `runningBatchKey`. As a result, when `getRunningBatchKey()` (or related logic depending on it) was invoked during the JUnit tree-building phase, the field was still `null` instead of an `Optional`, causing a `NullPointerException`. The fix addresses this by giving `runningBatchKey` a safe default value (`Optional.of("batch-1")`) at field declaration time, ensuring it is never `null` and can be safely used even before any batch is explicitly started.

Here is the patch:
     private TestContext testContext;
 
-    private Optional<String> runningBatchKey;
+    // must be initialized for jbehave-junit-runner
+    private Optional<String> runningBatchKey = Optional.of("batch-1");
     private boolean dryRun;

private Optional<String> runningBatchKey;

The field `runningBatchKey` is declared without an initializer, so it defaults to `null`. It is only assigned an actual `Optional` value when a batch execution starts through the normal Vividus runner flow. Since `jbehave-junit-runner` builds the JUnit execution tree before any batch execution begins, this initialization never happens in that flow. Consequently, any code invoking a getter or logic depending on `runningBatchKey` (e.g., `getRunningBatchKey()`) during the tree-building phase operates on a `null` reference instead of an `Optional`, resulting in a `NullPointerException`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
private Optional<String> runningBatchKey = Optional.of("batch-1");
Reason:
By initializing `runningBatchKey` with a default value (`Optional.of("batch-1")`) at declaration time, the field is guaranteed to never be `null`, even before any batch execution is explicitly started. This ensures that when `jbehave-junit-runner` accesses this field during JUnit tree construction (prior to actual story execution), it receives a valid `Optional` instance instead of `null`, thus preventing the `NullPointerException`.
